Cars travelled east and west on the top level of the bridge. Electric trains served other parts of the East Bay. The A Train covered downtown Oakland, and the B Train travelled through the Lakeshore and Trestle Glen neighborhoods. The E Train went to Berkeley to the Claremont Hotel. In Berkeley, the F Train travelled on Shattuck to Solano, the G Train served Westbrae, the H Train travelled on Monterey Avenue, and the K Train ran on College Avenue. Today, some AC Transit buses use the same letters to identify their routes. End of the Line The last Piedmont streetcar operated until 1948. With the proliferation of automobiles after World War II, electric streetcars were no longer considered efficient. Buses, later run by AC Transit District, took over the streetcar routes. The C Train continued to run to San Francisco until 1958 when streetcars on the Bay Bridge were discontinued. The Oakland Tribune described this poignant time as “sad, exuberant, quiet, noisy, confused and orderly.” That last ride was standing room only. Homeowners along the train’s route came out to wave goodbye, as the motorman saluted back. The C Train at the small Oakland Avenue station at Latham that provided shelter to waiting passengers in 1940. Legacy The Number 11 and 12 streetcar lines and the C Train also left a legacy of vacant right-ofway land. The right-of-way for the Number 11 between Sunnyside and Linda became the beautifully landscaped Linda Park and the energetic Linda Avenue Dog Park across from Beach School. The Number 12 streetcar on Fairview Avenue had no dedicated right-of-way. When the C Train stopped running, its right-of-ways were filled with houses. Today, three narrow houses occupy the right-of-way along Latham. The land between Ricardo and York became more back yard space for adjacent houses. New houses were built on York near Arroyo. The C Train also shared the right-of-way on Arroyo with the Number 10 streetcar before it turned onto Brandon Street and Piedmont Avenue in Oakland. Today, the north side of Arroyo and the south side of Ramona are filled with mid-century houses. The trail also surrounds you with the aroma of California Bays, the sprawling red bark of Manzanita, and A view of Swanson Creek. You’ll walk over the creek to continue on the Contour Trail. Triple Falls is our final of five thriving waterfalls in the park. It’s the tallest at around 50 feet. a towering second-growth redwood here and there. Intersecting with the Alec Canyon Trail, turn right to head just slightly less than a mile to Triple Falls, the final landmark of the day and the tallest of the waterfalls at around 50 feet, a small trickle compared to the other four. Our Uvas Canyon loop to hit every waterfall is approximately 5.2 miles and topped out at 1,273 feet in elevation gain. The Post passed 44 hikers on the day, but over 36 of which came on the initial walk on the Waterfall Loop given its popularity. It is also one of the few dog friendly parks in the Santa Cruz Mountains, so it is safe to bring your pooch without fear of repercussion. It’s also worth mentioning that 24 hour advance reservation for parking, otherwise you’ll be parking on the road leading in. The practice runs were also helpful for avoiding any potential failures on the track. “When you build a car, you’re never really sure if it’ll make it all the way down, so you want to run it at least once. A couple of my kids’ cars didn’t even make it down the first time, so the trial runs were very helpful,” laughed Pan. There were also learning opportunities for the girls that would pop up spontaneously during the fine-tuning of their cars, said Pan. “When the parents were helping children with tweaking the cars, they had the chance to explain to some kids why putting weight in the back of the cars is more advantageous than in the front, which was a good learning moment.” Pan was also excited about the potential turnout of the event. “We just sold our 97th car, and we only have one left in our supply! That means we have high participation this year.” Pan advised parents to make sure their kids eat before the race, but in case they don’t, Troop 33587 will also be holding a bake sale at the race. Proceeds will benefit their annual middle school graduation trip. The Girl Scout Pinewood Derby will be held in the Piedmont Community Church Education Building, 10 Highland Way, on Saturday, February 3, from 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. For more information, contact Carolyn Pan via email at carolynpan@yahoo. com.
